name: Kohima
description: Capital of Nagaland and headquarters of Kohima district, a hill city at about 1,261–1,444 m elevation on the foothills of the Japfü range. Historic Angami Naga settlement that became the scene of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima; base for Hornbill Festival, war cemetery, and access to Dzukou Valley and surrounding villages.
facts: Base for Hornbill Festival at Kisama

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in central Kohima, built on the battlefield of the 1944 Battle of Kohima. Contains 1,420 Commonwealth burials and a memorial to 917 cremated Hindu and Sikh soldiers; white concrete lines mark the historic tennis court where the fiercest fighting occurred. Famous epitaph: When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today.
facts: Tennis court marked on former DC bungalow site

name: Kisama Heritage Village (Naga Heritage Village)
description: Open-air heritage village 12 km south of Kohima between Kigwema and Phesama, designed as a traditional Naga village with morungs representing all 17 ethnic groups of Nagaland. Permanent venue of the annual Hornbill Festival (1–10 December) featuring cultural performances, crafts, food, and tribal architecture.
facts: 12 km south of Kohima on NH
Morungs of all 17 Naga ethnic groups

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, declared India’s first green village in 2005. Features terraced paddy fields, historic Semoma Fort from 19th-century resistance against the British, and the Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting the endangered Blyth’s tragopan. Community-led conservation with no hunting or logging.
facts: Protects Blyth’s tragopan in ~30 sq km sanctuary

name: Dzukou Valley (Dzükou Valley)
description: High-altitude valley at about 2,438–2,452 m on the Kohima (Nagaland)–Senapati (Manipur) border, behind Mount Japfü. Famous for rolling meadows of dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers including the rare Dzukou lily, streams, and trekking. Approached from Viswema or Jakhama villages; shared border landscape requiring care with district assignment.
facts: Known for Dzukou lily and rhododendrons
Trek from Viswema/Jakhama ~25 km from Kohima

name: Japfu Peak (Mount Japfü)
description: Second-highest peak in Nagaland at 3,048 m, part of the Barail Range about 15 km south of Kohima. Popular moderate trek from Kigwema village offering panoramic views of Dzukou Valley and surrounding hills; home to the world’s tallest rhododendron tree (Guinness record) and habitat for Blyth’s tragopan.

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima, established 1970 and operated by the Department of Art and Culture. Houses ethnographic collections of Naga tribal artefacts, textiles, weapons, jewellery, musical instruments, and traditional life from all major tribes of Nagaland.

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Roman Catholic cathedral on Aradura Hill in Kohima, consecrated 1991. Architecture incorporates traditional Naga house elements with a sweeping roof and carved timber; features one of Asia’s largest wooden crucifixes (16 ft). Largely funded by Japanese donors in memory of soldiers who died in the Battle of Kohima.
facts: On Aradura Hill overlooking the city

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small remote Angami Naga village in Kohima district about 30–40 km from Kohima, known for community conservation (no hunting/trapping since 1999), dense forests, terraced fields, clear streams, and eco-tourism homestays. Quiet offbeat base for nature walks and birdwatching near Khonoma.

name: Touphema Tourist Village
description: Community-based tourism model village about 36–41 km from Kohima, recreating a traditional Angami Naga settlement with thatched huts, morungs, and a small ethnographic museum. Offers overnight stays, local cuisine, cultural performances, and village walks; developed with Nagaland Tourism as a rural heritage experience.
facts: Model for rural tourism in Nagaland
